title: Word 4 — On Our Renunciations and Vows Made at Baptism
attribution_note: Word 4 of 28 in the collection Short Moral-Instructive Words — see Word 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: Holy Baptism is like a door, through which those being baptized enter the Holy Church and become close to God and fellow-citizens of the saints. But they do not enter simply, without more ado — before Baptism they utter renunciations and vows.

1) At that time we renounce Satan and all his evil works. Satan is a cunning and evil spirit; he was created good by God, but together with his fellow-conspirators fell away from Him, and so from bright became dark, and from good became evil and cunning. His works are these: idolatry, pride, cunning, lying, flattery, deceit, envy, malice, plunder, adultery, fornication, every uncleanness, slander, blasphemy, and every sin. For he is the inventor of sin; it was he who beguiled our first parents in paradise and led them into sin and falling away from God. It is this evil spirit and all his evil works that we renounce before Baptism.
2) We renounce all the vanity, pride, and pomp of this world, as those called and renewed unto eternal life.
3) We promise to serve Christ the Son of God, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, in faith and truth, and to follow in His footsteps.

4) In this way a covenant is established between God and us. Having renounced Satan, we promise to serve God and to be faithful to Him. God receives us into His most high mercy, and promises us the inheritance of eternal life and the kingdom, and washes us — defiled by sins — in the bath of Baptism, sanctifies us, and justifies us; therefore the priest greets every newly baptized person: *“Thou art washed, thou art sanctified, thou art justified”* [see 1 Corinthians 6:11].

Beloved Christians! Let us call to mind these renunciations and vows, and examine ourselves, whether we are keeping them. For it is a grievous thing to lie to God, and very dangerous to be found false before Him. Let us examine, then, whether any of us has turned back to Satan, has renounced Christ, and has forsaken Him. Let us examine on whose side we stand — Satan's or Christ's. For whoever does another's will serves him and belongs to him. It is not only the one who renounces Christ's holy name in words, and does not confess Him as the Son of God and his own Savior, who renounces Christ — but also the one who shamelessly and fearlessly breaks His holy commandments. This is apostolic teaching. For the apostle says: *“They profess that they know God; but in works they deny Him,”* and so on [Titus 1:16].
You see, then, that people renounce God not only with their lips, but with their deeds as well.
Whoever fornicates or commits adultery has renounced Christ and turned to Satan.
Whoever harbors malice against his neighbor and schemes how to do him harm has forsaken Christ and joined himself to the devil.
Whoever steals, plunders, or takes away his neighbor's goods has fallen away from Christ and gone over to Satan.
Whoever deceives or leads his neighbor into temptation is no longer with Christ, but with Satan, and so on.
All such people fail to keep the vows they made to God, and have therefore lied to God.

sections.heading: Choosing Christ's side, now and forever

pairs.en: Let us examine, then, beloved, our conscience and our life, and see on whose side we stand — Christ's or His adversary's, the good side or the evil, that of the saved or that of the perishing. Whoever is not with Christ is with the devil and stands against Christ. For Christ Himself says: *“He who is not with Me is against Me”* [Matthew 12:30]!

Beloved! Let us take heed and be with Christ here, in this world, as we promised at our Baptism. Let us be with Christ here, so that in the age to come we may also be with Christ, according to His unfailing promise: *“Where I am, there My servant will be also”* [John 12:26]. Let us serve Him here as our King and God, so that on the day of judgment He may acknowledge us as His servants, number us among His faithful slaves, and open to us the doors of eternal joy. Amen.
